sections.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
sections.abstract: For twisted genus-g GL(r) character varieties, the authors prove the Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas purity conjecture, expressing the graded dimension of pure cohomology through the Kac polynomial of a one-vertex, g-loop quiver.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.3 proves the purity conjecture and gives the pure part's graded dimension in terms of the Kac polynomial for the one-vertex quiver with g loops.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main setup is a twisted GL(r) character variety for a smooth compact surface of genus g at least 2, with r positive and d coprime to r.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns the pure part, not the full mixed Hodge polynomial, and its proof composes several recent P=W, P=C, and BPS-theoretic results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A named purity conjecture is stated as proved, with an explicit quiver/Kac-polynomial formula; the paper is cross-listed in algebraic geometry and representation theory, and its introduction and main theorem were inspected.

sections.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
sections.abstract: Every compact finite-rank nilspace embeds into a toral nilspace of the same step, and the authors use this to prove the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and obtain a Gowers-norm inverse theorem for second-countable compact abelian groups.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that each k-step compact finite-rank nilspace embeds continuously into a k-step toral nilspace, then derive the conjectured inverse theorem with connected filtered nilmanifold targets.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The inverse theorem is for 1-bounded Borel functions on second-countable compact Hausdorff abelian groups with a Gowers U^(k+1) norm bounded below by a positive parameter.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is qualitative: the finite target family and constants depend on k and the norm threshold, with no effective bounds stated in the abstract; the proof uses the general nilspace inverse theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper claims a proof of a named higher-order Fourier-analysis conjecture; its toral-embedding theorem is the stated structural step, with relevance across group theory, combinatorics, and dynamics. The introduction and theorem statements were inspected.

sections.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
sections.abstract: The authors construct compactly supported vorticity for an unforced, axisymmetric three-dimensional Euler flow without swirl that blows up in finite time, with initial velocity simultaneously in every C^(1,alpha) class for alpha below 1/3.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.1 constructs finite-energy initial data whose classical solution has a non-integrable-in-time vorticity supremum before a finite time T*.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The flow is unforced, axisymmetric, without swirl, on R^3; the initial velocity is smooth away from the origin, belongs to the intersection of C^(1,alpha) for 0<alpha<1/3, and has compactly supported vorticity.
sections.unique_caveat: The initial data is not smooth at the origin and the construction has no swirl; it does not establish blow-up from smooth data, which the authors identify as an open direction for axisymmetric Euler with swirl.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors state a sharp near-critical regularity result and give a specific multiscale blow-up mechanism; the main theorem and its hypotheses were checked in the paper's introduction.

sections.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
sections.abstract: The authors claim that every tracial ultraproduct of complex matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group, implying uncountably many nonisomorphic such ultraproducts and answering a question of Sorin Popa.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' abstract asserts triviality of the fundamental group for every tracial matrix ultraproduct and of its first-order fundamental group.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The objects are tracial ultraproducts of sequences of full matrix algebras M_n(C), with the fundamental group notions used in operator-algebra/model-theoretic settings.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is stated for matrix ultraproducts, not all II_1 factors; the arXiv comment calls this a first draft and invites comments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It states a resolution of a named operator-algebra question and a stronger first-order variant, with cross-listing in operator algebras, logic, and representation theory.

sections.title: A counterexample to Arveson's finiteness question for subdiagonal algebras
sections.abstract: The authors construct a maximal subdiagonal algebra in a type-II_1 von Neumann factor with scalar diagonal and uncountably many faithful normal conditional expectations, most of which are not preserved by any nonzero finite trace.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' construction shows that only the trace-associated expectation preserves the normalized trace, while the other expectations are not preserved by any nonzero finite trace, answering the 1967 question negatively.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A unital sigma-weakly closed subalgebra of a type-II_1 factor is considered, with scalar diagonal equal to the complex multiples of the identity.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract supplies a counterexample to the finiteness question, not a classification of all subdiagonal algebras or their conditional expectations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a concrete negative answer to Arveson's named finiteness question and an explicit operator-algebra construction, spanning operator algebras and functional analysis.

sections.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
sections.abstract: For the normalized complex polynomials in Smale's mean-value problem, the author proves that the supremum of the degree-wise constants is 4 and that the constants tend to 4 as degree grows, with a Lean 4 formalization of the main result.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves sup_d K(d)=4 and K(d) tends to 4, showing that Smale's upper bound cannot be replaced by any smaller uniform constant.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For complex polynomials p of degree d at least 2 with p(0)=0 and p'(0) nonzero, K(d) is defined from the minimum over the critical points of p.
sections.unique_caveat: Each individual K(d) remains strictly below 4, so the supremum is approached only as degree tends to infinity and is not attained at a finite degree.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract settles the sharp universal constant and gives an explicit construction; a Lean 4 proof artifact is linked in the arXiv comments.

sections.title: The four-dimensional Borsuk number is five or six
sections.abstract: For diameter-one sets in four-dimensional Euclidean space, the author proves six parts always suffice in a partition into smaller-diameter sets, while five are sometimes necessary, and formalizes the theorem in Lean.
sections.claimed_result: The author's abstract claims that the four-dimensional Borsuk number is either five or six: six always suffice, and there are sets for which fewer than five parts cannot suffice.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The problem concerns partitioning sets of diameter one in R^4 into subsets each of strictly smaller diameter.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper leaves the central binary question unresolved: whether five parts always suffice.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper improves the stated upper bound from seven to six and supplies a Lean 4 formalization deposited with the paper; Semantic Scholar reported one current citation (also marked influential), giving this item the only nonzero early citation signal in this selected set.

sections.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
sections.abstract: The authors prove that no free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to the three-generator free lattice FL(3), and report that the theorem is checked in Agda.
sections.claimed_result: The authors rule out the infinite chain in free lattices, while showing that without freeness FL(3) does contain an infinite ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The formal statement is for free lattices over generators with decidable equality; the authors report using Agda's safe flags and no classical principle.
sections.unique_caveat: The chain prohibition depends on freeness and is specific to copies of FL(3); the contrasting nonfree example shows the freeness hypothesis cannot simply be dropped.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It answers a question left open in earlier work, includes an Agda-checked main theorem and public formal development, and crosses lattice theory, group theory, and logic.

sections.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
sections.abstract: The author proves that the nth term of the recursively defined Ulam sequence is at most exp(O(sqrt(n))), improving the previous exponential-in-n upper bound using an additive-combinatorial covering lemma.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims an upper bound e^(O(sqrt(n))) for the nth Ulam number, replacing the previous exponential upper bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: This concerns the standard recursively defined Ulam sequence of positive integers; the abstract gives asymptotic order rather than an explicit constant.
sections.unique_caveat: The arXiv abstract explicitly says the proofs are due to ChatGPT; the mathematical argument therefore merits independent expert verification, and the O-constant is not specified in the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated growth bound substantially improves the prior upper bound and the proof uses a potentially reusable additive-combinatorial lemma; it is cross-listed in combinatorics and number theory.

sections.title: Counterexamples to the clamped-plate eigenvalue ratio conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors disprove Ashbaugh's conjecture that a ball maximizes the second-to-first eigenvalue ratio for the vibrating clamped-plate problem by constructing smooth connected counterexample domains in every dimension at least two.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show the eigenvalue ratio can be strictly increased beyond the ball's value, using perforated-domain approximations to their interior-sphere construction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the clamped-plate eigenvalue problem on smooth connected domains in Euclidean dimension at least two.
sections.unique_caveat: This disproves optimality of the ball but does not identify the maximizing domain or the sharp supremum of the ratio.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract reports a counterexample to a named spectral conjecture in every dimension d>=2 and describes a geometric construction that survives smoothing and connectivity constraints.

sections.title: The roads taken in the directed landscape
sections.abstract: In the directed landscape, the authors prove that almost surely every finite-length path spends all but a time set of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61 on the union of geodesic interiors, and construct paths with exceptional sets of dimension at least 1/3.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' abstract states the almost-sure 57/61 upper bound on exceptional-time Hausdorff dimension and a construction attaining at least 1/3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result is for finite-landscape-length paths in the directed landscape and holds almost surely with respect to its random environment.
sections.unique_caveat: The upper and lower bounds leave a substantial gap between 1/3 and 57/61 for the largest possible exceptional-set dimension.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper provides a sharp-looking quantitative structural statement with an explicit upper bound and a constructive lower example, using several named probabilistic-geometric estimates.

sections.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
sections.abstract: For a finite connected weighted graph with a unit voltage drop between two terminals, the author characterizes exactly when equality holds in the moving particle lemma and computes the resulting equality kernels for exclusion and interchange processes.
sections.claimed_result: The author shows equality is confined to representations with at most two rows, identifies the two nontrivial voltage/graph cases, and derives the full kernels through the regular representation.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The graph G=(V,c) is finite, connected, and weighted, with distinct terminal vertices and unit voltage drop.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification is for equality cases in this finite-graph setting; the abstract does not claim an extension to infinite graphs or other processes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives exact necessary-and-sufficient equality cases and a complete equality-kernel decomposition, with cross-listing across probability, mathematical physics, and combinatorics.
